title.narrative: VOSIEDA Climate Smart Agriculture for Resilience and Livelihood Support
VOSIEDA Climate Smart Agriculture for Resilience and Livelihood Support

description.narrative: Insatsen kommer att bidra till att minska klimatförändringarnas påverkan för de mest utsatta människorna, av vilka majoriteten är kvinnor som lever i fattigdom. Aktiviteterna är inriktade på att stötta småskaliga jordbrukare att anpassa och utveckla sina jordbruksmetoder, inklusive att främja användningen av organiska gödningsmedel framför kemiska, att förflytta sig från svedjebruk och på så sätt bidra till skydd av skog och bevarandet av viktiga kolsänkor

The initiative will contribute to reducing the impact of climate change on the most vulnerable people, majority of whom are women living in poverty. Activities are targeted at helping smallholder farmers adjust and improve their farming practices, including promoting the use of organic fertilizers over chemical fertilizers, moving away from shifting cultivation, thus, contributing to protection of forest, and preserving important carbon sinks.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and VOSIEDA

description.narrative:
The programme supported 47 farming groups with 3,503 beneficiaries, the majority of whom were women, strengthening gender and youth inclusion. According to VOSIEDA reports, farming groups received agricultural training, while youth-led teams provided services that created employment and improved farmer support. Coordination improved through quarterly stakeholder meetings, two joint monitoring missions, and a regional forum involving 50 government, civil society, and development partners.
Adoption of climate smart agriculture increased yields by 2530% for major crops, supported by drought and pest tolerant seeds and the establishment of on-farm composting sites. A shift to sustainable lowland farming reduced deforestation and protected 3,551 hectares, while climate awareness activities reached over 5,600 people. Six field technicians provided continuous advisory services on soil conservation, pest management, harvesting, composting, and agroforestry, contributing to over 2,000 hectares being managed using climate smart practices.
Farmer exchange programmes engaged 470 farmers, strengthening networks and local market opportunities. Eight youth-led agribusinesses were established to provide essential farm services, and two women-led processing facilities were launched, advancing women's economic empowerment. Across all communities, 47 VSLAs expanded access to savings and credit, with annual savings increasing from 950,000 LRD to 3.5 million LRD. Approximately 700 women reinvested in small businesses, while 580 women used savings to meet essential household needs.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
